entities.name: PMID:25430398
observations: Meldau, Wu, and Baldwin (2014) studied systemic SIPK activation and JA accumulation after Manduca sexta oral secretion or wounding in Nicotiana attenuata.

The study concluded that FAC-containing oral secretion is required in the wound-associated herbivory context for the tested systemic SIPK and JA responses; FACs alone were not established as sufficient.
Wounding alone produced no detectable systemic SIPK activation or systemic JA increase, whereas wounding plus oral secretion induced responses in selected undamaged systemic leaves.
Systemic responses were spatially selective, and broad systemic TPI induction could occur independently of systemic SIPK/JA elevation.

entities.name: Fatty acid-amino acid conjugates
observations: FACs in Manduca sexta oral secretion function as wound-associated herbivory elicitors for systemic SIPK activation and JA/JA-Ile accumulation in Nicotiana attenuata.
Their requirement is conditional on tissue damage and delivery into the wound; the study did not establish FACs as a standalone systemic trigger.

entities.name: SIPK
observations: Systemic SIPK activation was detected after wounding plus Manduca sexta oral secretion/FAC elicitation, but not after wounding alone in the tested Nicotiana attenuata design.

entities.name: Jasmonic acid accumulation
observations: Systemic JA and JA-Ile accumulation occurred in selected undamaged leaves after wound plus FAC-containing oral secretion, but was not detected after wounding alone.
